feedback.overall:
1. Overall assessment  
Strong senior digital communications CV with clear positioning, credible progression, and relevant public-sector scope. It reads polished and substantive, but it is slightly dense and repetitive, with a few style/grammar inconsistencies that reduce sharpness.

1. Top strengths  
- Clear leadership narrative: strong progression at NACo from coordinator to director, reinforcing credibility and growth.  
- Good impact signals: website scale, audience size, platform scope, and named tools make achievements believable and concrete.  
- Well-aligned branding: headline, competencies, projects, and technical stack consistently support the “digital platform & communications systems leader” profile.

1. Top improvements  
- Tighten repetition: themes like governance, workflows, editorial systems, and multi-channel operations recur across summary, competencies, experience, and skills. Consolidate to improve punch.  
- Add more outcome metrics: several bullets describe responsibilities rather than results. Include measurable gains where possible (engagement, efficiency, cost savings, adoption, search performance, production volume).  
- Fix style/grammar consistency: “social, and multimedia” should be “social and multimedia”; “Ranked among the top public universities…” is unnecessary filler; capitalization is inconsistent (“DAVIS” vs standard title case); punctuation/bullet formatting in experience and footer is uneven. No obvious spelling errors, but “A2/Learning” is stylistically awkward—use “A2 (learning)”.
feedback.intro:
Quick assessment: Strong, credible positioning that aligns well with the CV, but it’s slightly dense and repeats themes already covered in the subtitle, core competencies, and work experience. It would be stronger with sharper outcomes and a cleaner opening line.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Replace “building the platforms” with a more direct leadership framing: “Digital leader with 12+ years leading platform modernization, governance, and content operations for high-volume public-sector communications.”
- Tighten the second sentence by grouping related areas: “Leads enterprise web modernization, analytics and reporting infrastructure, editorial workflows, multimedia operations, and AI-enabled search and content experiences.”
- Consider adding scale or audience impact from recent roles if space allows, e.g., “10,000+ page websites” or “mission-driven organizations serving national audiences.”
- Standardize style: use either “12+ years’ experience” or “12+ years of experience”; both are fine, but keep phrasing crisp.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “AI-enabled user experiences” overlaps with core competencies and recent projects; “AI-enabled search and content experiences” would be more specific.
- “Complex, mission-driven organizations” is broad and somewhat generic given the stronger public-sector specificity elsewhere.
feedback.coreCompetencies:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant themes, but this block overlaps heavily with the header and Topline Skills. It would be more effective if tightened into broader, less repetitive capability areas with sharper wording.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Consolidate overlapping items and reduce phrase length for faster scanning.
- Use parallel noun phrases and consistent scope across all bullets.
- Emphasize highest-value, recent strengths: web modernization, governance, analytics, AI/search, automation, and multimedia.
- Suggested rewrite: Enterprise web modernization • Digital governance and editorial operations • Analytics, reporting, and insight infrastructure • AI-enabled search and content discovery • Workflow automation and platform integration • Multi-channel public-sector communications • Multimedia production and livestream operations

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Advocacy and public-sector communications” overlaps with the header and Topline Skills; consider keeping only “public-sector communications” here.
- “Digital governance & editorial systems” and “Multi-channel communications operations” are already echoed in Topline Skills and multiple roles.
feedback.footer:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant project snapshot, but it reads dense and overlaps with work-experience bullets. Tightening phrasing and emphasizing outcomes, scope, or distinguishing details will make it feel more additive.

Suggested rewrite improvements:
- Add a one-line intro such as “Selected recent projects” and keep each item to one crisp sentence with parallel structure.
- Replace generic verbs like “Built”/“Developed” with more specific ones where possible: “Launched,” “Architected,” “Produced,” “Delivered.”
- Clarify impact or scale where available: audience, campaign purpose, platform complexity, or organizational use.
- Standardize style: use “AI-enabled,” “Drupal 10,” and “10 x 20-foot” consistently; consider “bill-level AI assistant” instead of “bill-level AI chat.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- AI Hybrid Search, microsite development, and advocacy video series closely repeat current freelance/NACo experience; make this section more project-specific or outcome-focused to avoid restating role bullets.
- “Organization Anniversary Campaign” is the most distinct item; use it as a model for showcasing unique project work not covered elsewhere.

items.title: CV Footer
items.content:
### Recent Projects
**AI Hybrid Search**
Designed an AI-enabled legislative search experience combining hybrid retrieval, structured content workflows, vector search and bill-level AI chat to improve discovery of complex policy content.
**We Are Counties Microsite**
Built a Drupal 10 campaign microsite with custom navigation, interactive storytelling modules, downloadable resources and a modular structure designed for continued campaign growth.
**Organization Anniversary Campaign**
Developed a multi-part digital campaign combining editorial storytelling, archival media, web features and a 10×20-foot interactive conference display connected to the main site.
**Advocacy Video Series**
Built a recurring advocacy video program spanning editorial planning, production and distribution across website, email and social channels.

items.title: Strategic Communications Consultant
items.subtitle: Freelance (full-time engagement)
items.content:
Support a U.S.-based national membership organization on digital strategy, campaign platforms, content operations and enterprise web improvement.
- Build and refine digital systems, workflows and analytics that support coordinated organization-wide communications.
- Develop campaign and storytelling experiences within the organization’s Drupal platform, including custom microsite structures, modular content sections and downloadable member-facing toolkits.
- Deliver CMS development, front-end implementation and technical troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Advise on governance, usability and operational best practices across web, email, social and multimedia channels.
- Lead development of an AI-enabled search initiative, shaping retrieval strategy, structured content workflows and user-facing discovery design.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant current role, but it reads as a task list and overlaps heavily with the header, competencies, and NACo entries. Tighten it around 3–4 high-impact contributions and add outcomes or scale wherever possible.

Suggested edit
- Open with scope + client type: “Embedded consultant for a U.S. national membership organization, leading digital platform strategy, campaign delivery, and web operations improvement.”
- Replace generic verbs (“support,” “advise”) with ownership verbs: led, built, launched, redesigned, standardized, improved.
- Consolidate into impact-focused bullets, e.g.:
- Built Drupal campaign and storytelling experiences, including microsites, modular content components, and downloadable member toolkits.
- Improved communications operations by redesigning workflows, analytics, and governance across web, email, social, and multimedia channels.
- Delivered front-end/CMS enhancements and troubleshooting for large public-facing web properties.
- Led an AI-enabled search initiative covering retrieval design, structured content workflows, and user discovery experience.
- Add metrics if available: number of sites/pages, users, publishers, campaign launches, time saved, search success, or engagement lift.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “AI-enabled search” and the microsite work already appear in Recent Projects; keep this entry higher-level.
- Governance/analytics/platform modernization also echo the NACo role—emphasize what is new or more advanced here.

items.title: Director of Digital Media
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led NACo’s digital communications team, overseeing the organization’s website, email, social media and video platforms, along with digital strategy, analytics, governance and budget management.
- Led the redesign and migration of NACo’s 10,000+ page website into a new Drupal platform supporting 3.5 million annual page views, 6,000+ average daily users and 50+ internal publishers.
- Directed NACo’s core digital communications channels, including email newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and social media platforms serving thousands of followers.
- Built NACo’s first broadcast-quality in-house video studio, expanding in-house capacity for advocacy programming, event production and recurring multimedia content.
- Expanded the organization’s analytics infrastructure across GA4, Microsoft Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio and BigQuery, improving reporting and strategic decision-making.
- Strengthened digital operations through clearer governance, publishing standards and cross-department planning systems.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, high-impact leadership entry with solid scale metrics. Tighten the opening, foreground the biggest transformation work, and add outcome language so it reads less like a scope summary and more like a results-driven director role.

Suggested edit
- Replace the first sentence with a sharper headline: “Directed NACo’s digital communications function across web, email, social, video, analytics, governance, and budget management.”
- Lead with the website achievement and outcome: “Spearheaded redesign and migration of a 10,000+ page website to Drupal, supporting 3.5M annual page views, 6,000+ daily users, and 50+ internal publishers.”
- Make channel leadership more specific and measurable: include newsletter volume/open-rate growth, audience growth, campaign performance, or production cadence if available.
- Combine operations/analytics bullets for concision: “Built enterprise reporting across GA4, Clarity, Power BI, Looker Studio, and BigQuery, while formalizing governance, publishing standards, and cross-department workflows.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- “Email/social/video operations” overlaps with the 2018–2022 role; keep this entry focused on director-level transformation, infrastructure, and team leadership.
- Video studio/buildout may overlap with footer project examples; keep one concise bullet here and let projects show detail.

items.title: Associate Communications Director
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content:
Led day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social media and video, helping scale NACo’s editorial coordination and advocacy communications.
- Managed four recurring weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.
- Produced and expanded a weekly advocacy video update, helping establish video as a recurring policy communications channel.
- Strengthened editorial planning and coordination across communications, advocacy and program teams.
- Helped improve the consistency and effectiveness of NACo’s digital publishing workflows.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression story, but this item is too close to the later Director role and earlier Digital Media Manager role. Make it more execution-focused and specific about what changed under your leadership.

Suggested edit:
- Open with scope + function: “Managed NACo’s day-to-day digital communications operations across web, email, social and video, coordinating editorial delivery for advocacy, program and member communications.”
- Tighten bullets around distinct outcomes: “Managed four weekly newsletters reaching tens of thousands of county officials and public-sector stakeholders.”
- Reframe video bullet to show channel-building impact: “Produced and scaled a weekly advocacy video update, establishing video as a recurring policy communications channel.”
- Combine workflow/editorial bullets: “Built stronger cross-team editorial planning and more consistent digital publishing workflows across communications, advocacy and program teams.”

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Led day-to-day digital communications operations” overlaps with the Director role’s broader channel oversight; keep this item focused on execution and coordination, not enterprise leadership.
- Weekly video/livestream language also overlaps with the 2015–2018 role; emphasize scaling and formalizing the program here.

items.title: Digital Strategy & Content Leadership
items.content:
- Enterprise digital strategy
- Editorial systems and governance
- Multi-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector and advocacy messaging
- Audience-focused content planning
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong positioning, but this skills block overlaps heavily with the header and Core Competencies. It should be tighter, more distinctive, and framed around senior-level leadership themes rather than repeating generic phrases.

Suggested edit:
- Replace with sharper, less repetitive wording:
- Enterprise digital strategy & modernization
- Editorial governance, publishing systems & workflow design
- Cross-channel communications leadership
- Public-sector, membership & advocacy communications
- Audience strategy, content planning & message architecture
- Consider swapping “Multi-channel communications leadership” for “Cross-channel communications operations” if you want stronger alignment with recent roles.
- Use parallel noun phrases throughout; avoid mixing broad concepts (“messaging”) with process terms (“planning”).
- If space allows elsewhere, tie this section to scale by adding context in experience bullets instead of here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Enterprise digital strategy” and “Editorial systems and governance” duplicate both the header and Core Competencies almost verbatim.
- “Public-sector and advocacy messaging” overlaps with Core Competencies’ “Advocacy and public-sector communications.”

items.title: Web Platforms & Technical Execution
items.content:
- Drupal
- WordPress
- SharePoint
- Power Pages
- CMS modernization
- HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery
- API integrations
- Workflow automation
- Airtable systems
- AI-enabled search experiences
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong category, but it reads like a raw tool list and overlaps heavily with the “Technical + IT” section. In Topline Skills, this should emphasize higher-value platform leadership and current strengths, not repeat every technology.

Suggested edit:
- Reframe from tools to capability clusters: “Drupal & CMS modernization • Front-end implementation (HTML, CSS, JavaScript) • API integrations & workflow automation • Airtable-based systems • AI-enabled search experiences”
- Drop lower-priority or older items unless they are target-role keywords; keep Drupal first, and consider removing jQuery.
- If SharePoint/Power Pages matter for target roles, group them as “Microsoft web platforms” rather than listing both separately.
- Use parallel phrasing and fewer items; aim for 5–6 max to keep this section scannable.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates “Technical + IT > Web Platforms & CMS” and “Coding & Technical Implementation”; Topline Skills should stay more strategic.
- “CMS modernization,” “workflow automation,” and “AI-enabled search experiences” already echo Core Competencies, so keep wording distinct.

items.title: Analytics, Insights & Optimization

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This overlaps heavily with “Technical + IT > Data, Analytics & Optimization”; consider making this section more strategic and that section more tool-specific.
- “Leadership reporting” is weaker than “executive dashboards” or “executive reporting.”

items.title: Multimedia Production & Event Delivery

items.title: University of Virginia
items.subtitle: Bachelor of Arts (BA), Economics & History
items.content: Ranked among the top public universities in the United States
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: The current line adds little value and reads like generic school marketing. For an experienced candidate, this education entry should be minimal and factual unless you have honors or distinctions worth adding.

Suggested edit:
- Replace the content line entirely with no body text; the degree, school, location, and dates are sufficient.
- If applicable, swap in a concrete credential instead: “Relevant coursework: …” or “Honors: …” only if genuinely strong and still relevant.
- Tighten the subtitle to “B.A., Economics and History” for cleaner formatting.
- Consider dropping dates if you want to reduce age signaling and keep focus on recent senior experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Ranked among the top public universities…” is generic and not candidate-specific, so it weakens the entry rather than strengthening it.
- Avoid adding coursework unless it clearly supports current digital strategy/communications work; otherwise it will feel disconnected from the stronger recent experience.

items.title: Web Platforms & CMS
items.content: Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as a generic keyword dump and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. This item should either be tightened to emphasize strongest/recent platforms or reframed to show level of use.

Suggested edit:
- Prioritize the most relevant/recent tools first: **Drupal • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- If space allows, add light qualifiers to show depth: **Drupal (enterprise migration, microsites) • WordPress • SharePoint • Power Pages • GitHub Pages**
- Consider renaming the heading to be more specific: **CMS & Web Platform Administration** or **CMS Platforms**
- If you want more impact, move lower-value/older tools like GitHub Pages to the end or drop it if not central to target roles

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This largely duplicates **Topline Skills > Web Platforms & Technical Execution**; keep the list here shorter and let the other section carry broader technical keywords.
- “CMS modernization” is already covered elsewhere, so don’t repeat it in this item.

items.title: Coding & Technical Implementation
items.content: HTML5 • CSS3 • JavaScript • jQuery • API integrations • Google Tag Manager • Cloudflare Workers • GitHub Actions
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid technical coverage, but this reads as a generic keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Web Platforms & Technical Execution” in Topline Skills. Tighten it to emphasize implementation tools actually used in recent roles and group items more clearly.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as: “Front-end implementation: HTML5, CSS3, JavaScript, jQuery”
- Add a second grouped phrase: “Technical delivery: API integrations, Google Tag Manager, Cloudflare Workers, GitHub Actions”
- If accurate, replace older/generic items with stronger recent specifics, e.g. “Drupal front-end theming,” “CMS troubleshooting,” or “search/API implementation” to better match current consulting work
- Consider dropping version numbers (“HTML5,” “CSS3”) unless the rest of the skills section uses version-specific naming

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- Duplicates “HTML, CSS, JavaScript and jQuery” and “API integrations” already listed under Topline Skills
- “Workflow automation” appears elsewhere; avoid implying GitHub Actions is a major differentiator unless supported by project bullets

items.title: Automation & Workflow Systems
items.content: Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Basecamp • Slack • Teams • Trello
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid tool coverage, but this item reads as an undifferentiated software list and overlaps with “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” elsewhere. Tighten it to emphasize systems you actively build with and separate automation platforms from collaboration tools.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Automation, Workflow & Collaboration Tools**
- Reorder by relevance/strength: **Airtable • Power Automate • Zapier • Jira • Asana • Slack • Microsoft Teams • Trello • Basecamp**
- If accurate, add light qualifiers to show depth, e.g. **Airtable (workflow databases) • Power Automate/Zapier (process automation) • Jira/Asana (project workflows)**
- Consider trimming lower-value/general tools if space is tight; keeping 6–7 strongest platforms will feel more senior than a long list.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Workflow automation” and “Airtable systems” already appear in Core Competencies/Topline Skills; avoid repeating the same phrasing here.
- Slack and Teams are common workplace tools; unless used for structured workflow operations, they add less differentiation than automation/build tools.

items.title: Email & Engagement Systems
items.content: Dynamics 365 Customer Insights / Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid platform list, but it reads as generic software inventory rather than evidence of email/engagement capability. Since email leadership already appears in recent NACo roles, this item should stay concise and platform-focused without repeating channel management claims.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to: **Email Marketing & Member Engagement Platforms**
- Tighten platform names for readability and consistency: **Dynamics 365 Customer Insights – Journeys • Higher Logic • Mailchimp**
- If accurate, add one capability cue instead of more tools: **campaign automation, newsletter operations, audience segmentation**
- Keep only platforms you’ve used meaningfully in recent roles; if one was light exposure, remove it to strengthen credibility

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid adding “email newsletters,” “tens of thousands of recipients,” or audience-growth language here; that impact is already covered in Work Experience
- “Engagement” may overlap with broader “Multi-channel communications operations” in Core Competencies, so keep this item narrowly tool-based

items.title: Data, Analytics & Optimization
items.content: GA4 • Microsoft Clarity • Looker Studio • Power BI • BigQuery • SEO • A/B testing • Dashboarding
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong, relevant tool stack, but this item is currently a flat keyword list and overlaps heavily with “Topline Skills.” In a technical section, tighten it into clearer capability groupings and avoid generic terms that are already implied elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite as grouped, cleaner phrasing: **GA4, Microsoft Clarity, BigQuery • Looker Studio, Power BI • SEO analysis • A/B testing • KPI dashboarding**
- Replace **Dashboarding** with **KPI dashboarding** or **executive reporting dashboards** for more specificity.
- If truthful, sharpen **SEO** to **technical SEO** or **SEO/performance analysis** to better match senior-level work.
- Consider dropping one BI tool only if space is tight elsewhere; keeping both is fine because the NACo role explicitly supports both.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This nearly duplicates **Topline Skills → Analytics, Insights & Optimization**; consider trimming that section or making this one tools-only.
- “A/B testing” is not evidenced in work history; keep only if you can support it in interviews or add a related outcome elsewhere.

items.title: Work Eligibility
items.content: Full legal authorization to work in Belgium (Visa D + residence permit / carte de séjour)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Useful for Belgium-based applications, but the phrasing is a bit legalistic and takes more space than needed. This should read as a clear status note, not a headline achievement.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite for brevity and recruiter scanability: “Authorized to work in Belgium (Visa D and residence permit).”
- If accurate, make it stronger and simpler: “Fully authorized to work in Belgium; residence permit in place.”
- Avoid the French term unless the role specifically requires bilingual administrative terminology; “residence permit” is usually enough.
- Consider moving this into the contact/header area for local applications, since eligibility matters more there than in a secondary rail.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- No major duplication, but this item is lower-value than recent experience; keep it very short so it doesn’t compete for attention.
- If location/contact already signals Belgium and applications are local, this may be optional rather than essential.

items.title: Languages
items.content:
**English** (Native)
**French** (A2/Learning)
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item is clear but too compressed and visually awkward. It should be reformatted for quick scanning and framed honestly so French supports your Belgium-based role without overstating proficiency.

Suggested edit
- Rewrite as a simple line: Languages: English (native) | French (A2, currently improving)
- Use lowercase proficiency style for consistency and cleaner tone: native, A2, conversational/basic if accurate.
- If relevant to target roles, add practical context only if true: French (A2, professional working improvement underway)
- Keep it concise; this section is supporting information, not a selling point versus your recent digital leadership experience.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings
- No major duplication, but avoid overdesign/bolding here; the CV already has strong skills sections competing for attention.
- If space is tight, this can stay in the rail and should not be repeated in the header, summary, or cover letter unless language is job-relevant.

items.title: Soft Skills
items.content: Cross-department coordination • Stakeholder communication • Team leadership • Strategic planning • Clear writing and editing • Problem-solving • Adaptability
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This section is too generic and largely repeats strengths already proven in the summary and core competencies. On a senior CV, “soft skills” should either be removed or reframed as leadership traits tied to scope and outcomes.

Suggested edit:
- Rename to “Leadership Strengths” or “Management & Collaboration” to sound more senior and less filler.
- Cut generic items like “Problem-solving” and “Adaptability”; keep only traits that support target roles.
- Tighten to 4–5 items max, e.g.: Cross-functional leadership • Executive stakeholder management • Editorial judgment • Team development • Strategic planning
- If space is tight, remove this section entirely and use the room for quantified achievements in recent roles.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Cross-department coordination” and “Stakeholder communication” duplicate the header summary and Core Competencies.
- “Team leadership” and “Strategic planning” are already demonstrated more credibly in the 2022–2024 Director role.

items.title: References
items.content: References available upon request.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: This item adds little value and uses space that could better support recent, higher-impact experience. “References available upon request” is assumed by most employers and usually should be removed.

Suggested edit:
- Delete the “References” entry entirely.
- Use the freed space for stronger supporting content instead, such as a brief “Selected Results” rail item with 1–2 metrics from recent roles.
- If references are specifically requested, provide them separately rather than on the CV.
- If you want a replacement rail item, consider “Work Authorization” or “Languages,” which are more useful and already present here.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- This section is redundant because reference availability is standard and does not differentiate you.
- Keeping it may weaken the second-page rail by displacing more relevant, recent qualifications.

items.title: Digital Media Manager / Producer
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Advanced through two digital roles, supporting the creation of the organization’s first in-house digital team and strengthening workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia. Contributed to a major website refresh and produced high-impact digital content—including livestreams and weekly video updates—while providing day-to-day guidance to a digital media associate.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Strong progression signal, but the item is too broad and overlaps with the 2018–2022 and 2022–2024 NACo roles. Make it more foundational: emphasize team-building, early digital operations, and specific outputs rather than repeating later leadership themes.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground scope and progression: “Promoted across two digital roles to help build NACo’s first in-house digital team and establish workflows across web, email, social, and multimedia.”
- Add concrete outputs if available: website refresh size/traffic, number of livestreams or weekly videos produced, audience reach, or production cadence.
- Tighten the close: “Produced livestreams and weekly video updates and provided day-to-day oversight to a digital media associate.”
- If metrics are unavailable, use operational outcomes: improved publishing speed, more consistent cross-channel delivery, or expanded in-house production capacity.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- “Strengthening workflows” and “weekly video updates” overlap with the 2018–2022 role; frame this entry as the setup/build phase.
- Avoid repeating website leadership language already covered more strongly in the 2022–2024 director role.

items.title: County Solutions & Innovations Coordinator
items.subtitle: National Association of Counties
items.content: Coordinated innovation and research projects supporting organizational programs and policy work. Contributed to digital content production and multimedia materials, and launched the organization’s first podcast, overseeing planning, scripting, and production.
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid early-career entry, but it reads generic and overlaps with later NACo digital/media roles. Emphasize the podcast launch as the clearest differentiator and tighten the research/program support language.

Suggested edit:
- Rewrite to foreground the unique achievement: “Coordinated innovation and research initiatives supporting NACo programs and policy priorities, while contributing to early digital content and multimedia production.”
- Make the podcast launch the second sentence and sharpen ownership: “Launched NACo’s first podcast, leading concept development, episode planning, scripting and production.”
- Replace vague phrasing like “supporting organizational programs and policy work” with more specific internal stakeholders or outputs, if possible.
- Add any measurable outcome available: number of episodes, audience growth, internal adoption, or how the podcast supported advocacy/member engagement.

Duplicate/redundancy warnings:
- Avoid overemphasizing digital content production; later NACo roles already cover multimedia, video and channel operations in much stronger detail.
- Don’t repeat team-building or workflow language used in 2015–2024 roles unless this role truly introduced those systems.

items.title: Multimedia & Creative Tools
items.content: Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream studio workflows • Podcast production
items.aiFeedback:
Quick assessment: Solid supporting skills list, but it reads more like a mix of software and capabilities. Tighten it to emphasize current, professional production tools and avoid repeating broader multimedia themes already covered elsewhere.

Suggested edit:
- Rename/reshape for consistency: **Premiere Pro • Audition • Photoshop • Illustrator • Livestream production workflows • Podcast production**
- If space allows, make the capability terms more specific: **Livestream studio operations** or **Broadcast-quality livestream workflows** instead of the vaguer “Livestream studio workflows.”
- Consider separating tools from production capabilities for cleaner scanning, e.g. **Adobe Premiere Pro • Adobe Audition • Adobe Photoshop • Adobe Illustrator • Livestream production • Podcast production**
- Only keep Photoshop/Illustrator if you actively use them in recent roles; otherwise prioritize the video/audio items most aligned with your 2022–present leadership work.
